notes.title: Mark Hamill To Host ‘Thunderful World’ Digital Showcase on November 10th
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37569367/892bc383a39eb0b46c5b4b09af85c4f9f1be9298.jpg[/img]

Hey friends,

we have some awesome news, which we can finally share with you today: We - that's Thunderful Games - welcome all of you to the premiere of our very first digital games showcase ‘[b]Thunderful World[/b]’! ːsteamhappyː

Find out more in the following press release:


[i][b]Gothenburg, Sweden - October 28th, 2021[/b] - International developer and publisher Thunderful Games, creator of the multi-award winning and multi-million selling SteamWorld franchise, is welcoming everyone to a new digital games showcase, ‘[b]Thunderful World[/b]’. The event will be taking place on [b]November 10th at 11am PT / 2pm ET / 7pm GMT / 8pm CET[/b], hosted by Hollywood and pop culture icon [b]Mark Hamill[/b]. Tune in to the livestream on Twitch, YouTube and the [url=https://thunderful.world/][b]thunderful.world[/b][/url] website.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37569367/8a01bc9ec10d1ba6e674354314fd34accd1fbb51.png[/img]

Tune in to see Mark delight us with a ton of exciting new game reveals and announcements from Thunderful. The event will deliver updates on exciting upcoming titles including the surprise indie hit of Summer Game Fest, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1608230/Planet_of_Lana/][b]Planet of Lana[/b][/url]. There will also be more news on Thunderful titles like [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1608550/Firegirl_Hack_n_Splash_Rescue/][b]Firegirl[/b][/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1726120/Cursed_to_Golf/][b]Cursed to Golf[/b][/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1315610/Source_of_Madness/][b]Source of Madness[/b][/url], [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1276660/Tinkertown/][b]Tinkertown[/b][/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1158890/White_Shadows/][b]White Shadows[/b][/url]. 

Alongside Mark’s headline hosting role, the event will also feature appearances from Thunderful Group CEO Brjánn Sigurgeirsson, Corporate Vice President at Xbox Sarah Bond, plus a few other surprise industry partners.

Thunderful is proud to be partnering with Xbox and The MIX for Thunderful World. To sign up for the event and be the first to know all the important information ahead of the show on [b]November 10th[/b], head over to [url=https://thunderful.world/][b]thunderful.world[/b][/url]. As your one stop shop for all things Thunderful World, the website will be updated with new announcements and reveals as the event unfolds.[/i]


Stay tuned and tune in on Nov 10th - see you all in the event!
Your Thunderful Games-Team

notes.title: Patch 1.01 reaches the finish line!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/4ade7604ede7cedab261c27ef05dc244fb494ada.png[/img]

Hi there,

Over the past few weeks some kind people of our [b]Doodle Derby[/b] community pointed out a couple of bugs in the game. I am very happy for this feedback and did my best to fix these things as soon as I could. Please stay alert and report any issues you might find and I will check it out and fix things.

[b]So let’s just call this Doodle Derby v1.01.[/b] ːsteamhappyː

[b]What where the issues?[/b]
[list]
[*] After collecting a map you would lose all your single player progress. Unfortunately we can’t recover any progress you might have lost.
[*] The second issue was that uploading a level to mod.io would give an error. This is now fixed and you can start sharing your wildest creations. Looking forward to seeing them.
[/list]

[b]How was this possible?[/b]
Well, without becoming to technical, when you fix things in a game or implement some optimization, sometimes, new bugs slip in. Things we missed. So again, please stay alert and let me know on the community discussions when you find something suspicious.

Thank you all for playing! ❤️

Cheers,
Erikson

notes.title: We made it: Doodle Derby v1.0 is here!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/f655424dc958db2aef7b05d01b490511f1562079.jpg[/img]

Hi there,

The past few weeks have been exiting and weird. Finalizing the game and getting it ready for the final release. I’ve been working on it day and night for the past three years. So this moment is something I visualized many times, a dream come true. And here we are [b]Doodle Derby[/b] has left Early Access!

[b]Thank you![/b]
The creation of this passion project was a hell of a ride. It sure wasn’t without bumps and I had to learn a lot along the way. It was a struggle to get visibility and recognition. The support of friends, family and you has been incredible helpful and supporting. You gave me the energy to push forward in stressful times when work kept piling up.

[list]
[*] I would like to thank all the people who helped out testing the game since the very buggy beginning. Thanks for your bug reports and suggestions. This was invaluable feedback and brought the game where it is today.
[*] Thanks to all content creators for your videos, articles and streams. Thanks to everyone who helped spread the word.
[*] Thanks to my family for dealing with my absence and supporting me in such an incredible way.
[*] Thanks to Headup for your trust and passionate effort to spread the word.
[*] Thanks to my awesome team of super committed volunteers and freelancers who helped me in ways I can’t describe.
[*] And finally thanks to all the people who bought the game.
[/list]

[b]The 1.0[/b]
It took me 3 years. It was a blast. And here it is version 1.0. [b]Fromto: Toy Cars in Hell[/b] became [b]Doodle Derby[/b]. And now we are leaving Early Access. This opens the game up to all the players who just won’t play early access games, which is very understandable. Now as the game is at 1.0 we are also ready for the release on Nintendo Switch. Yeah!

Enjoy the game, buy it if you haven’t already. I mean it’s the price of a fancy cup of coffee. ːsteamhappyː

Cheers,
Erikson


https://store.steampowered.com/app/916180

[b]Doodle Derby v1.0 release notes:[/b]
[list]
[*] 12 new steam achievements.
[*] World records and your rank on the leaderboard is shown per single player level.
[*] localization update: Missing translations and overlapping text issues are resolved.
[*] Some UI improvements.
[*] The game now uses 3d sound.
[*] Sync projectiles in tank battle mode in a better way.
[*] General optimization to make the game run as smooth as possible.
[*] Medal sprites updated.
[*] Switch version done
[*] Some improvements on the level editor
[*] Mod.io functionality improved and updated.
[/list]
[b]Bug fixes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Elevator sound bug.
[*] fix a bug where the game would act as a tank battle in race mode.
[*] Fixed the thing where you could pause the game at the start of a single player level and start driving while paused. This way you could reduce your time drastically.
[*] Fixed the thing where the timer could occasionally be negative.
[*] Fixed a thing where you could get an error when a gamepad was lost.
[/list]

notes.title: Doodle Derby Update #4: A giant leap!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/76f9e82e60cb1179e2614f6b6fe60a66d46be325.png[/img]

Hello there!

I hope everybody is doing well in these strange and scary Corona times.
Although it has been quiet the past few weeks around [b]Fromto[/b], this doesn’t mean we have been standing still. On the contrary I would say. We have been working really hard to take the game to the next level. We feel this update is a giant leap forward.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/c51ec89ce74fefd3ca121f849ff94a2b4efa8020.jpg[/img]

[b]Big changes, new name.[/b]
We decided that from the moment of this update ‘[b]Fromto[/b]’ will get an entirely new name: ‘[b]Doodle Derby[/b]’. We feel that [b]Doodle Derby[/b] has more appeal to it and reflects the game better.

[b]More game for less money.[/b]
We lowered the price of the game so all those people, currently sitting at home, can start playing the game right away without any hesitation. If you already own the game, you will get a copy for free. It will be added to your steam account. So you can give it to a friend and double the fun!

[b]Here is a summary of the new stuff:[/b]
[list][*] A new game mode: Tank battle!
[*] The single player challenges are done
[*] General optimization for better performance
[*] Pimped multiplayer levels
[*] New fancy backgrounds
[*] Menus have been updated
[*] New ‘ultra noob’ setting to flatten the curve
[*] Improvements, additions and changes on multiple track elements
[*] Some bug fixes
[*] localization update
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/ac7e638e207c2a5cea60d0066f8c4c12df0232fc.jpg[/img]

[url=https://discordapp.com/invite/doodle-derby]Join our Discord[/url] to meet me and other players and share your experience, ideas and feedback.
Discord.gg/doodle-derby

I am super exited for this update and hope you are too.
Enjoy!

Erikson

notes.title: New Keyboard UI Update is live!
notes.content:
Hi there!

Here I am with another small [b]Fromto[/b] update. It came to my attention that many people are playing the game with the keyboard (of course). Some of you had problems with remapping keys and no wonder… There were some loose ends in the remapping system. So I decided to take the time to make this work properly. In addition, I upgraded the UI so the controls are displayed more clear in game:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/8cf2ef4eb1e691e634c48171bfba805a9f4178ac.png[/img]

I am working on the new levels for the single player campaign. This takes time to do it right. 
I will let you know when the next batch arrives. For now, I added one extra level to play around with.

[h1]Here is what has changed with this keyboard UI update:[/h1][list][*] I changed the default keyboard mapping to something that works better
[*] (You can manually rebuild the previous setup, if you prefer the old one)
[*] The controls remapping system should work now properly
[*] You can now actually save your custom controls setup
[*] There is a double check now when choosing a key which is already in use
[*] The in game controls help system got a paint job and looks much clearer
[/list]
[h1]Other things:[/h1][list][*] Single player level 8: I gave a bit more points to spend in the shop and some easier track parts as it seemed too hard for some in this stage
[*] Added one extra single player level (more to come!)
[*] Changed the Font for Arabic users
[/list]
[h1]Lastly:[/h1][list][*] The design an “[url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/916180/announcements/detail/1687091057809541510][b]Evil Level Challenge[/b][/url]” is still on. I am really hoping to see your creation!
[*] You can win the extra steam key to give away to a friend
[*] [b]Deadline: Friday the 13th! So go on! Just try it![/b]
[/list]

Cheers,
Erik

notes.title: Let's (Remote) Play Together!
notes.content:
Hello you all!

Today I want to point out a very cool new Steam feature! Maybe you’ve already heard about it. Maybe not. It's [b]Steam Remote Play Together[/b]!

Steam has started a beta a few weeks back which allows you to play your favourite local multiplayer games online! This means you can easily connect with your Steam friends to play games as if they were sitting next to you. So this is supercool! Even cooler is that it will work with [b]Fromto[/b] right from Early Access release. ːsteamhappyː

What is the difference with the regular online multiplayer mode in [b]Fromto[/b]? Well in this case you will be streaming your monitor to the others. In [b]Fromto[/b]’s ‘all together’ race mode online the camera will only follow you where in local play everybody must be on screen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/d605013a917ee1bbab61f3b8b0bba08e509a9a86.gif[/img]
[i]Play with or play your friends?[/i]

But the main difference is that you would need only one copy to play with your friends.
This is available since last week or so for every Steam user. Here is some more info:

https://steamcommunity.com/games/593110/announcements/detail/3032537193879549687
So I would say a good opportunity to check out [b]Fromto[/b] with some friends starting this Thursday…

[b]Only 3 days left![/b] ːsteamhappyː

Cheers!
Erikson

notes.title: 5 Days left till the Carpocalypse begins!
notes.content:
Hey you!
Let me start with a capital [b]OMG![/b]

Only 5 days left till [b]Fromto: Toy Cars in Hell[/b] will launch in Early Access! This is my first release ever so I am currently eating a broom stick to calm my nerves.

To ease my pain I decided to write a little story about why I think Fromto is so cool.

One of the coolest things in Fromto are traps. While trying to build a road to the finish together you must make sure you get there first. So you use traps to make it hard. But then again you need to be able to make it. Or not? Maybe the fun lies in obstructing the people who are so handy with their controllers. Beat this giant car munching gorilla! (Meanwhile you created another path the others weren’t paying attention to.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/a4d6cebd94450358f493655444caec89eace7583.gif[/img]
[i]Speaking about a car munching gorilla?[/i]

notes.title: Welcome to the Fromto Early Access Feature Hightlight!
notes.content:
Hi there!
Early Access is only three weeks away. So let's highlight a few cool things that will be within the Early Access release version.

[b]The core gameplay[/b]
In [b]Fromto: Toy Cars in Hell[/b] you must build the track before trying to reach the goal of the level. You will start off as a little helicopter, collect crates and use the items inside to pave your way to the finish. After building you can try to make it to the finish in a hell of a ride. Can’t do it? Rebuild it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/2a45c7caa6c0966e1f128f2c1b186b8d48af65fc.png[/img]

[h1]Highlighting some Early Access release features:[/h1]
[b]2 Multiplayer Modes[/b][list][*] [b]Race in turns:[/b] the traps YOU place won’t harm you, but they will be a pain for the rest.[*] [b]Race together:[/b] you can crash against each other. Push them of the cliff![/list]
[b]Singleplayer Campaign Chapter 1 [/b]
Combine your brains with your skills to earn gold medals on all levels. (about 20 levels)

[b]Gameplay Customization[/b]
Customize your multiplayer game with your own gameplay settings. (modifiers)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34364550/16847a294b65d33cac49d0c58b76b01ce11ba5ac.gif[/img]

[b]Level Editor[/b]
Build your own multiplayer map in minutes and play / share them instantly.
Download and play maps build by the community.

See ya all on the tracks at the [b]Fromto: Toy Cars in Hell[/b] Early Access release on 14th of November!
Cheers!
Erik

notes.title: Fromto on Track for Early Access on November 14th!
notes.content:
Hey guys! It's been a little while since my last update, but no worries! We are still alive and kicking! Today we have some exciting news to share.

We have been pimping this devilish ride with great dedication and focus. We added a multiplayer mode were you can race together! Another added feature is the level editor where you can show of your level design skills. Basically the whole game got a fresh new paint job. We implemented a lot of community feedback and are excited to show it to you all.

So we are inviting all of you to joining us for the Steam Early Access launch on [b]November 14th[/b]. Why Early Access? The answer is very easy: We want to listen to your feedback and use this to finalize the game to perfection in the last stretch of the development.

The Early Access release will include the first chapter of the single player campaign (about a third of the full campaign), multiplayer and level editor. (See the full feature list under ‘features’.) More features will be implemented during the Early Access.  We will post a roadmap with the global plan here soon.

Cheers!
Erik


[b]PS.[/b] We have decided to remove the Party Crash demo. This will happen within a couple of days. I feel that the demo has become redundant and outdated.

notes.title: The Fromto demo is a lot of scribbly, messy party platformer fun
notes.content:
Scribbly party puzzle platformer Fromto isn’t out until later this year, but its dad-and-his-kids dev team just rolled out a demo on Steam to test your friendships. Reminding me of anarchic platformer Transformice (although Studio Erikson cite Ultimate Chicken Horse, Worms and Trackmania as inspirations), it’s a local or online multiplayer platform racer. Drive your bouncy car around a 2D maze, hit checkpoints, then to the finish line. Unfortunately the track is incomplete, and after reach round of failures, players get a chance to place roads and traps to help and hinder.

notes.title: Fromto #1: Making a horribly childish game!
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34364550/9c029dbf8986b79bdc15762ff23fef5f2589b61f.gif[/img]

My daughter Niki hands me another drawing. I take the drawing and find an empty spot on the floor to lay it to dry. When I look around I see the whole studio floor and all chairs, and desks covered with dozens of artworks from my kids. In the middle of it the two of them are drawing and painting with their tongues between their teeth. The studio is next to the house where we live. So, it is a kind of extension of their playground. Although it is quite normal for a dad to play or make drawings with his kids, I believe we took it to the next level. We are working together on a game. We are making the background art for upcoming sandbox party racing game [b]Fromto[/b]. 

[h1]From the beginning the whole concept of working with my kids, using their untamed expression, seemed super logical.[/h1]

I have a background as a contemporary artist. A Pigheaded one, even for contemporary artist’s standards. Always just following my gut. Making giant ugly installations, sculptures for the public space, paintings, drawings, animations, comic books, you name it I tried it. I never really felt at home in the world of Art with a capital A. As a result, a few years ago I decided to jump in the world of game development. It took years to master the coding and all the other skills needed. I tried to stay in the art scene with one foot for a while, but it just didn’t fit anymore. The change resulted in little income from some side jobs, so it took even more dedication and patience from my family (my wife Marijn in particular). But after a few years of studying and experimenting I felt confident enough to start working on a real game. I had plenty ideas on the shelves, but made the mistake of thinking too big. I was alone, and I had to come up with something doable. When I realized that, the idea of [b]Fromto[/b] came along.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34364550/965721ba30544a7df68166aeb087d1a33ef18eaa.jpg[/img]
[i][b]The Fromto blueprint drawn by Erik in his early days[/b][/i]

When my kids started to make their first drawings (scribbles) I wondered how my own childhood scribbles looked like. I went to my parents and they gave me several boxes with many drawings that I made in my early days. While going through them I found a drawing that triggered the idea for [b]Fromto[/b]. Well, actually it is a blueprint for [b]Fromto[/b] – a drawing of a small race car going through an obstacle course on one sheet of paper. Awesome!

At that moment everything fell into place. I was going to make a game, a childish game. The way kids play with toy cars in a sandbox was going to be the experience. And to emphasize this childish aspect I would ask my kids to draw the backgrounds. And I would draw the rest of the game in a doodle scribble style to glue it all together.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34364550/70a577f43f535aa416dcb29bba0aa719ed9208ef.jpg[/img]
[i][b]Eriks children creating background art for Fromto[/b][/i]

I never wrote it down in a game design document whatsoever (Pigheaded artist). No, I was going to do it may way. I just started working on it, created some track parts, some doodle cars, some basic controls and there we go. Let’s play! From that point in time it took me almost two years to make it the game it is today. By trial and error. Test and improve, listen to advice from friends and use inspiration from other games.

One of the games I played a lot with friends is Worms Armageddon. Therefore, you might could get the same kind of vibe in [b]Fromto[/b]. [b]Fromto[/b] became a ‘turnbased strategic racing’ game because of that, I think. All players race an unfinished track in turn. When everyone fails all players must ‘work together’ to modify the track before they try again. Think strategic, build sneaky routes and trick your opponents with nifty traps and obstacles. Experiment endlessly with tons of track parts and win in unthinkable ways. Another inspiration is Ultimate Chicken Horse where players also can modify the level in game and race to the finish. 

[b]Fromto[/b] is the result of a creative process almost the same as making a piece of Art. I believe [b]Fromto[/b] became my masterpiece (If I may say so myself) because all the pieces of the puzzle just fitted together so well.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34364550/5be9294bcbe58ded2fbc34a370a30cb7e8302730.jpg[/img] 

The pieces of art my kids made had to be filtered. By now they have created over 500 drawings, but  for the game I had to scale down to about 80. The first selection we did together. This was difficult because I wanted more abstract works. My daughter, who is starting to draw more figuratively, wants puppets, trees and stick figures in [b]Fromto[/b]. I truly love those too; however, the game is already pretty chaotic and I felt it was better to stick to abstract scribbles. It must be weird for her. The other kids from school starting to dislike these ugly scribbles and I love them. I sometimes wonder if she would be drawing differently if I hadn’t encouraged the expressive scribble style so much. Joep is now 2 years old and totally knows what I am talking about.

The last two years became increasingly busy and the amount of work started to grow as the game’s potential became clearer. Ironically, I spend less time with my family as before. My day with the kids became a workday. I am glad that the studio is next door and that my kids can barge in at any time.

[h1]I am super proud of them and hope that you can experience their childish super powers in Fromto.[/h1]
